title: How Big AI Can Fit on Your Phone
description: How quantization stores AI model weights with fewer bits, trading a little precision for a much smaller memory footprint that can fit on a phone.
topic: Neural network quantization from 16-bit weights to 4-bit integers on mobile hardware

sources.name: Dettmers et al., LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
sources.supports: Quantization trades numeric precision for memory while preserving model quality.

sources.name: Hugging Face Transformers quantization overview
sources.supports: Describes 8-bit and 4-bit weight quantization used to reduce model memory footprint.

sources.name: Frantar et al., GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
sources.supports: 4-bit post-training quantization of large transformer weights with limited accuracy loss.

beats.narration: A powerful AI model can need more memory than a phone can spare.
That is why even a fast phone can struggle before the model answers.
The trick is to shrink the numbers inside the model, not throw the model away.
With four bits, each weight has sixteen possible values instead of thousands.
Think of a smooth mountain rebuilt from blocks: the shape stays recognizable.
Those smaller weights can cut memory use dramatically, though some accuracy may be lost.
That trade-off is what lets more AI run right on your phone.
